title: Muhammad and the Revelation
objective: After this level you can explain what Muslims believe about Muhammad and the revelation that began in 610, and why the hijra of 622 starts the Islamic calendar.
summary: Muslims believe that in 610 the angel Gabriel ordered Muhammad to recite; Khadijah was the first to believe, and the hijra of 622 became Year 1 of the Islamic calendar.

cards.headline: A cave, a voice and one command: "Recite!"
cards.body: In 610, Muhammad of Mecca was meditating in a cave on Mount Hira. Muslims believe what happened there began the Quran. A journey twelve years later became Year 1 of the Islamic calendar.

cards.headline: The night of "Recite!"
cards.body: Muhammad was born about 570 in Mecca. Muslims believe that in 610, as he meditated in a cave on Mount Hira, the angel Gabriel came to him and ordered him to recite. Words came that Muhammad believed were God's own. The revelations kept coming for the rest of his life, and, remembered and written down, they became the Quran.

cards.headline: The first to believe
cards.body: Khadijah, a merchant who had hired Muhammad to lead a caravan to Syria and later married him, is often considered the first person to believe his message. She reassured him that his first revelations were real. Then he began to preach: there is no god but God, and life should be lived in submission to God's will. That is the word itself. Islam means "surrender", and a Muslim is one who surrenders to God's will.

cards.headline: 622: Year One
cards.body: The message drew crowds, and Mecca's powerful saw Muhammad's popularity as a threat. In 622 he and his followers migrated north to Yathrib, later called Medina. Muslims call this move the hijra, "migration", and it mattered so much that the Islamic calendar counts its years from it. Muhammad led the young community until his death in 632.

mascot.line: Two dates, easy to swap. 610 is the first revelation; 622 is the hijra, and Year 1 of the Islamic calendar.

cards.headline: A messenger, not a god
cards.body: Remember Level 8's Abrahamic family? Muslims see Muhammad as the last in a line of prophets that includes Adam, Noah, Abraham, Moses, Solomon and Jesus. The Quran presents him as a human being with no divine qualities. In Islamic tradition he is God's messenger and the "seal of the prophets": the last of the line, not an object of worship.

cards.headline: Muhammad and the Revelation: the takeaways
learned: Muslims believe the revelation began in 610 on Mount Hira
Khadijah was the first to believe Muhammad's message
The hijra of 622 is Year 1 of the Islamic calendar

questions.prompt: According to Muslim belief, what happened in a cave on Mount Hira in 610?

options.label: Muhammad led his followers out of Mecca
The angel Gabriel ordered Muhammad to recite
Khadijah hired Muhammad for a caravan
options.rationale: That came years before the revelation.

options.label: Muhammad received the whole Quran at once
options.rationale: The revelations kept coming for the rest of his life.

questions.explanation: Muslims believe Gabriel came to Muhammad and ordered him to recite; the revelations continued for the rest of his life.

questions.prompt: How does the Islamic calendar count its years?

options.label: From Muhammad's birth in Mecca
options.rationale: The calendar starts with a journey, not a birth.

options.label: From the first revelation on Mount Hira
options.rationale: That was 610; the calendar starts in 622.

options.label: From the hijra, the migration to Medina in 622
From Muhammad's death in 632
options.rationale: The calendar starts ten years before his death.

questions.explanation: The hijra mattered so much that the calendar counts its years from it: 622 is Year 1.

questions.prompt: Level 8 placed Islam in the Abrahamic family. Which Muslim belief about Muhammad fits that family?

options.label: He is the last of a line of prophets including Abraham
He is worshipped as a divine son of God
options.rationale: The Quran presents him as human, with no divine qualities.

options.label: He was the first prophet God ever sent
options.rationale: Adam, Noah and Abraham came before him.

options.label: He replaced Abraham as the ancestor of Muslims
options.rationale: Muslims trace their line through Abraham's son Ishmael.

questions.explanation: Muslims see Muhammad as the last in a line of prophets that runs through Abraham, Moses and Jesus.
